messages.subject: EQS Elliptical Estimators in Lavaan
parts:
Dear all, 
I am trying to replicate an analysis that was done with EQS using an Elliptical estimator. I have come to realize that this type of estimator is only available to EQS. On the other hand I saw the mimic ="eqs" option on the fit function and I was wondering if there was a way to specify the elliptical model using the existing family of estimators supported by lavaan. 
Has anyone found anything alternative to that that can give me the same results?

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: EQS Elliptical Estimators in Lavaan
parts: I saw the mimic ="eqs" option on the fit function and I was wondering if there was a way to specify the elliptical model using the existing family of estimators supported by lavaan.

mimic ="eqs" only tells lavaan to make some output similar to EQS (e.g., how to calculate standardized residuals and SRMR, whether to use N or (N - 1) when calculating SEs and chi-squared).  According to p. 8 of the EQS manual, elliptical estimation is unique to EQS, but it is just another form of weighted least squares (WLS) with a particular weight matrix.  If you can figure out how to calculate that weight matrix (WLS.V) with the rows/columns arranged as lavaan expects (see ?lavaan help page), you can pass it to lavaan:

myWeightMatrix <- { something amazing }
fit <- lavaan(model = mySyntax, data = myData,
              estimator = "WLS", WLS.V = myWeightMatrix)

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Postdoctoral Researcher, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
